evidenceNotes: Lifetime total covers 82 observed short-form posts across YouTube, Instagram and TikTok. X, Twitch, FACEIT, unavailable archives and longer videos are not included. Historical views are separate from campaign growth and are not attributed to $0 new spend.

Starting measurement, October 11 at 2:51–2:53 AM Eastern: 31 public YouTube Shorts held 14,895 lifetime views; 33 Instagram Reels held 13,337 displayed lifetime views. These opening counters are not campaign gains.

The opening YouTube/Instagram measurement was about 23 minutes after campaign start; that gap and unmeasured posts remain unknown. TikTok is counted from its verified campaign-time creation. Paid-versus-organic attribution and unique audience size are not established.

October 11, 9:29–9:31 AM Eastern: net +337 YouTube and +68 Instagram views from opening counters, plus 280 views on the new TikTok post. The partial total of 685 is up 88 from the previous 597. Native downward counter revisions remain included.
Revenue remains unknown until confirmed payment records are connected. A support click or enquiry is not a payment.

The operator made no purchases, ad buys or paid media-generation orders for this campaign: recorded new spend is $0. Existing equipment, subscriptions and historical promotions are outside this new-spend figure.
Seven finished videos have 14 confirmed cloud schedules: YouTube daily at noon Eastern October 11–17, and Instagram daily at 6 PM Eastern October 12–18. Scheduled does not yet mean published.
The 17-slot rule counts active plus scheduled platform posts. Historical posts stay public in the archive. Two newly published posts plus 14 scheduled posts use 16 slots; one remains available.
The previews are editorial selections, not measured winners. Performance highlights are selected after publication and a four-hour review, with later checks for delayed analytics.

Owned source discovery covers Twitch recordings, local OBS footage and a 12-page FACEIT library. Three FACEIT originals and recovered Twitch clips supplied this batch. Complete archive indexing remains in progress.

First four-hour reviews completed October 11 at 7:27 AM Eastern. Readings were collected at ages 4.28 hours for TikTok and 4.27 hours for X. The later 24/72/168-hour checkpoints remain scheduled. One local publication-to-review cycle is verified; continued operation requires the PC and app to remain available.
X analytics at 7:26 AM Eastern showed 3 video views, 1 unique video viewer and 4 post impressions. Small video counts may include operator verification and remain excluded from the displayed total.

Four-hour review: TikTok has 279 views, 6.52 seconds average watch time, 10.2% full-video completion and its largest drop at 2 seconds. A tighter-opening test is commissioned from this retention signal. No winning format is established.

Legacy review at 7:25 AM Eastern: Come On, Code (+151 views) and Lurk King (+91) lead observed growth among 25 YouTube Shorts dated October 9. This spans about 4 hours 33 minutes of observation. Exact publication ages, source lineage for editing and attribution remain unverified.
